title: Gale–Ryser condition for bipartite degree sequences
statement:
Let $p=(p_1,\dots,p_m)$ and $q=(q_1,\dots,q_n)$ be sequences of non-negative integers with equal total, $\sum_{i=1}^{m} p_i = \sum_{j=1}^{n} q_j$, and suppose $q$ is non-increasing, $q_1 \ge q_2 \ge \cdots \ge q_n$. Then $(p,q)$ is realisable by a simple bipartite graph if and only if
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{k} q_j \;\le\; \sum_{i=1}^{m} \min(p_i,\, k)
\qquad\text{for every } k = 1, 2, \dots, n.
\]
hypotheses_covered: p and q are sequences of non-negative integers
the total of p equals the total of q
replaced:
(Gale--Ryser; Ryser, 1957). \emph{Let \texttt{p = (p$_{1}$, \dots{}, p\_m)} and
\texttt{q = (q$_{1}$, \dots{}, q\_n)} be sequences of non-negative integers satisfying
\texttt{$\sum$ p$_{i}$ = $\sum$ q$_{j}$} (11.16) and \texttt{q$_{1}$ $\ge$ q$_{2}$ $\ge$
\dots{} $\ge$ q\_n} (11.17). Then \texttt{(p, q)} is realisable by a simple bipartite
graph if and only if}

$\sum$\_\{i=1\}\textasciicircum{}\{m\} min\{p$_{i}$, k\} $\ge$
$\sum$\_\{j=1\}\textasciicircum{}\{k\} q$_{j}$ for 1 $\le$ k $\le$ n. (11.18)
